articles.title: Is Ravens QB Lamar Jackson Playing Against Browns In Week 6?
articles.summary: Ravens superstar QB Lamar Jackson will miss a second straight game this weekend against the Browns due to his ankle injury.
articles.body: Lamar Jackson will miss a second straight game this weekend because of his ankle injury. Coach Jesse Minter said Friday that Jackson would not play Sunday at the Cleveland Browns (Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX). Tyler Huntley led the Ravens (4-1) to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons last weekend. Huntley also won both his starts for Baltimore last season. Jackson was hurt while taking a sack near the end of the first half in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. The Ravens held on to win that game. Jackson missed four games last season, and Baltimore went 2-2 without him. The two defeats were started by Cooper Rush before the team turned back to Huntley, who had returned for another stint with the Ravens. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Millonarios 2027: la lista de refuerzos y las posiciones que buscará Alberto Gamero

articles.summary: El Embajador trabaja en el equipo del próximo año con varios puestos en la mira
articles.body: Aunque Millonarios se encuentra enfocado de lleno en los retos definitivos de la presente temporada, en los escritorios de la institución azul ya se trabaja con la mirada puesta en el futuro. La dirección deportiva y el cuerpo técnico encabezado por Alberto Gamero han comenzado a trazar la hoja de ruta para el armado del plantel de cara a 2027, con la firme intención de sumar jerarquía, equilibrio y variantes en posiciones estratégicas. De acuerdo con la información revelada por el periodista Guillermo Arango en La FM, la dirigencia de Millonarios tiene mapeadas tres zonas específicas del campo que considera urgentes de potenciar de cara al próximo año: La planificación de las nuevas caras para 2027 también coincide con un momento de decisiones administrativas complejas con varios elementos de peso en la plantilla actual, cuyos contratos expiran a finales de año. Figuras de peso y referentes del club como el capitán David Mackalister Silva, junto a nombres importantes como Sergio Mosquera, Danovis Banguero, Leonai Souza, Carlos Darwin Quintero, Julián Angulo, Rodrigo Contreras y Stiven Vega, se encuentran bajo la lupa de la gerencia deportiva para definir quiénes continuarán en el proyecto y qué bajas se oficializarán en el corto plazo. La expectativa entre la hinchada empieza a crecer ante los primeros movimientos del mercado de fichajes. El objetivo de la directiva es claro: blindar el proyecto deportivo con las piezas necesarias para que Alberto Gamero cuente con una nómina competitiva que responda a la alta exigencia de la hinchada tanto en el rentado nacional como en los escenarios internacionales.

articles.title: Dietmar Hamann asegura que Luis Díaz está fuera de forma en el Bayern
articles.standfirst: El ex del Bayern lanza dura crítica con el estado actual de Luis Díaz, quien solo ha podido hacer dos goles en la presente campaña
articles.summary: El ex del Bayern lanza dura crítica con el estado actual de Luis Díaz, quien solo ha podido hacer dos goles en la presente campaña
articles.body: El rendimiento del extremo colombiano Luis Díaz en el Bayern Múnich vuelve a estar en el centro del debate europeo. Las críticas más recientes han llegado de una voz más que autorizada en el entorno del gigante alemán, el exjugador Didi Hamann, quien analizó el presente del atacante y aseguró sin rodeos que el ‘cafetero’ se encuentra actualmente fuera de su nivel óptimo de forma. Tras deslumbrar en su primera etapa con el conjunto bávaro —donde registró cifras de absoluto destaque con 26 goles y 23 asistencias en 51 partidos—, el panorama actual de Díaz en la temporada 2026-2027 dista mucho de aquel brillo inicial. En lo que va del curso, el extremo colombiano ha disputado nueve encuentros oficiales en los que apenas ha podido inflar las redes en dos ocasiones y no registra asistencias. A esto se le suma una cuota considerable de mala fortuna y precisión milimétrica, con varios goles anulados por fuera de lugar que han cortado su ritmo ofensivo. Para Hamann, la merma en el impacto del colombiano sobre el terreno de juego es evidente, señalando que "está fuera de forma" y al equipo le cuesta encontrar variantes determinantes en el uno contra uno por la banda cuando el extremo no logra pesar en los metros finales. "El Bayern se está volviendo demasiado dependiente de Olise. Si él no hace nada, ¡nadie más lo hará! Es un jugador excepcional. Ni siquiera quiero imaginar qué pasará sin Olise si está de baja durante un periodo prolongado", señala Hamann. A pesar de los cuestionamientos externos de figuras históricas como Hamann, la interna del Bayern Múnich mantiene la calma y el respaldo hacia el extremo de la Selección Colombia. Directivos y cuerpo técnico han apuntado a que el jugador mantiene una actitud participativa en los circuitos de juego y confían en que recuperará su versión más desequilibrante a medida que avance el calendario europeo. El propio futbolista ha tenido que lidiar con cargas físicas exigentes, lo que incluso lo llevó a ausentarse de algunas convocatorias recientes con el combinado nacional para gestionar los esfuerzos de la temporada. El reto para Luis Díaz pasa ahora por revertir las valoraciones de la crítica alemana, recuperar la finura de cara al arco rival y consolidarse de nuevo como el socio ideal en el ataque del cuadro bávaro.

articles.title: Ryan Day Buyout: What Would It Cost Ohio State To Fire Its Football Coach?
articles.summary: Here's how much it would cost for Ohio State to buyout head coach Ryan Day's contract.
articles.body: Ryan Day became the first Ohio State head coach to lose to Indiana since John Cooper in 1988. If the Buckeyes lose again on Saturday in Bloomington, Indiana, he'd be the first Buckeyes head coach in the last 113 years of Ohio State football to lose consecutive games to the Hoosiers. Despite leading the Buckeyes to win the 2024 College Football Playoff less than two years ago, that losing streak to the Hoosiers could cause concern. Combine that with a 2-4 record against Michigan – a game that means more to many Ohio State fans than winning the national title – Day's time in Columbus could be nearing an end. But after signing a seven-year contract extension through the 2031 season, what would it cost for Ohio State to fire its football coach now? Ohio State would have to fund the remaining $75 million that Day is guaranteed over the next five-plus years of his contract. After leading the Buckeyes to defeat Notre Dame in the 2024 national championship game, Ohio State rewarded Day with a five-year, $87.5 million deal. Not only did he help them win the title, but they navigated the first 12-team playoff to get there, defeating Oregon and Texas before taking down the Fighting Irish. In the following season, Day led Ohio State back to the Big Ten championship game for the first time since defeating Northwestern in the COVID-shortened 2020 season, where they fell 13-10 to Indiana. Still, they received a bye in the first round of the CFP, but lost in the quarterfinals to 10-seed Miami in the Cotton Bowl. Overall, Day holds an 87-13 record at Ohio State. He's won two Big Ten Championships and a CFP national championship. But with his inability to consistently defeat Michigan, a potential second consecutive defeat to Indiana could spell his demise. articles.body:
One of three ranked SEC matchups this weekend is #13 Missouri (5-1) headed to Oxford, MS for a battle with the #9 Ole Miss Rebels (4-1). Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 last week following the bye week and couldn't have looked more crisp. Missouri on the other hand smoldered Texas A&M 27-6 and ran for more yards (247) than the Aggies had as an offense (216). Missouri is 7-1 all-time against Ole Miss as the last meeting was in 2019. Ole Miss' lone win in the series came in 1974, 10-0!

We can surely expect more than 10 points in this game as both offenses looked good last week. Missouri has ran for 467 yards and five touchdowns over the last two weeks with Jamal Roberts totaling 433 of those yards and all five scores. Ahmad Hardy has not returned to practice, so it's been an opportunistic year for Roberts.

This game is also a headliner quarterback Austin Simmons following his transfer from Ole Miss. Simmons has been fantastic for Missouri. He has a 14:1 TD to INT ratio after tossing his first pick of the season last week, plus a 64.8 completion percentage and 1,474 yards. Simmons was injured at Ole Miss and never saw the field as a starter for the Rebels again. Simmons was replaced by Trinidad Chambliss and we all know how that turned out.

If the season ended today, Ole Miss would more than likely be in the college football playoff. The Rebels outgained Vanderbilt in yards last week 409-343 and forced four turnovers. The Rebels defense had its best showing against a P4 opponent holding the Commodores to 2.8 yards per carry, four punts, and two turnover on downs.

The offense received a boost with Kewan Lacy returning to the lineup. Lacy ran for 39 yards and a touchdown on seven carries in the first half as Pete Golding eased him back into action. The Rebels ran for 196 yards and three scores, while Trinidad Chambliss accounted for one of those on top of airing it out for three touchdowns and 213 yards. Ole Miss looked like a contender out of the bye week, but Missouri is a step up in completion and playing well with their 1-2 punch of Simmons and Roberts.

Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us.

Missouri ran impressive in the win over Texas A&M. The Tigers ran for 247 rushing yards and the Aggies had 216 as a team. Missouri scored on five out of 10 drives starting from the second quarter and Jamal Roberts had back-to-back 200-yard rushing performances. Roberts is the hottest running back in the country right now with 211 and 222 rushing yards against Florida and Texas A&M, along with five touchdowns. Roberts has four games of 100-plus yards this season and scored in five out of six games.

Missouri Player to Watch on Offense: QB Austin Simmons

Austin Simmons is set for a revenge game against Ole Miss and the guy who replaced him; Trinidad Chambliss . This will be fun! Simmons has looked great for Missouri and threw a season-high 340 yards against Florida two weeks ago. Simmons has four multi-touchdown games and tossed three scores against Kansas and Mississippi State. He wasn't asked to air it out early in the season, but over the past three games he's averaged 32.3 pass attempts per game compared to 22.6 in the first three weeks. If Jamal Roberts can't find running lanes, then Simmons will surely be dropping back 30-plus times and looking to take matters into his own hands late. Simmons has 11 rushing attempts on the season and hasn't scored a touchdown on the ground yet. He's a sneaky anytime touchdown bet.

Versus a DI opponent, Missouri allowed a season-low in yards last week to Texas A&M at 216. Only 27 of those yards came on the ground as the Aggies were held to 1.2 yards per carry and no touchdowns. Missouri picked off Marcel Reed twice and held him to 19-of-39 (48.7%). Missouri ranks tied for 13th nationally with 3.0 sacks per game and ranks tied for 9th with 18 sacks on the season. The Tigers grabbed three sacks last week are they're coming into the week at 31.2% on third downs (26th). Missouri held Texas A&M to 4-of-18 last week on third downs (22.2%). Missouri will be bringing the pressure, but Chambliss thrives under duress. It should be a fun to watch the chess match between Missouri's edge rushers and Chambliss.

Missouri Player to Watch on Defense: EDGE Deaden Hopkins

Deaden Hopkins has only played in four out of Missouri's six games, but boy has he made his presence felt. Hopkins has at least a 0.5 sack in all four games, including Texas A&M last week. Hopkins had a career-high 3.5 sacks at Mississippi State after posting 1.5 sacks versus both Troy and Kansas, plus a forced fumble and recovery in both too. If you catch yourself going "who was that" or "that was close to being offsides"; it's probably Hopkins off the ball you're talking about.

articles.title: Welsh Cup: TNS among five Cymru Prem sides into third round
articles.summary: The New Saints survive a late scare to beat Airbus Broughton UK 2-1 and advance to the 2026/27 Welsh Cup third round.
articles.body:
The New Saints survived a late scare to beat Airbus Broughton UK 2-1 in the first all-Cymru Premier tie of the season and advance to the 2026/27 Welsh Cup third round.

Dan Williams scored late to ensure the current Cymru Premier leaders were not dealt an upset defeat after Jordan Evans cancelled out Dan Davies' early strike.

TNS were knocked out in the third round by Cardiff Met last season, and could draw the Students again after their 4-0 triumph over Ynyshir Albions.

Fellow top-flight sides Connah's Quay Nomads, Cambrian United and Briton Ferry Llansawel are also in the hat for the third round.

Connah's Quay, two-time winners of the competition, beat Porthmadog 4-0 while Cambrian United beat Trethomas Bluebirds 5-0, with Dylan Edwards scoring twice.

Briton Ferry Llansawel cruised past Afan United with Luke Bowen scoring a 16-minute hat-trick, and goals from Joseph Lloyd and Corey Hurford in a 5-0 win.

Bowen was not the only man to score a second-round hat-trick as Tim Parker fired three for Caerau Ely in their 6-0 dismantling of Cymru South strugglers Llanelli Twn.

Swansea-based Rockspur Fords edged a seven-goal thriller against Evans & Williams, winning 4-3 thanks to a decisive fourth goal from Daniel Williams.

Bangor City 1876 are also through to the third round after beating Cymru North rivals Denbigh Town 2-0.

Further second-round ties are set to take place on Saturday and Sunday.

articles.title: Atlético Madrid have already made a call on on-loan Jonathan David’s future
articles.summary: The brass at La Liga giants Atlético Madrid have already seen enough to make a definitive call on the long-term future of Jonathan David with the club.This c...
articles.body:
The brass at La Liga giants Atlético Madrid have already seen enough to make a definitive call on the long-term future of Jonathan David with the club.

This comes amid the understanding that the Rojiblancos are ready to do whatever it takes to make the Canadian international's signing a permanent one.

Frontman David of course swapped Italy for Spain this past summer. Out of favour at Serie A heavyweights Juventus, the 26-year-old was snapped up by Atlético on a loan deal through next summer.

David has since gone on to impress in the colours of his new employers, to the tune of five direct goal contributions in four La Liga appearances.

And as alluded to above, if the latest word stemming from the Spanish media is anything to go by, such production has already proven enough to convince those behind the scenes at the Metropolitano of the attacker's place in the club's long-term vision.

'The club are already exploring options to secure the striker's services permanently. All indications are that if an agreement isn't reached on the payment method or amount, Atlético are prepared to pay the full fee (€25 million). Furthermore, a portion of next season's budget has already been set aside for this transfer.'

articles.title: Lakers vs. Nuggets: What to watch in preseason finale
articles.summary: The Lakers close preseason against the Nuggets with two starting spots unsettled, availability questions and rebounding issues to address.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have one more preseason game to work through their questions before the results begin to count.

Friday's finale against the Denver Nuggets offers another opportunity to evaluate the two open starting spots, address rebounding concerns and potentially get several players back on the floor.

Practice brought encouraging updates this week, but availability will determine how much JJ Redick can learn from his final preseason look.

So here are three things to watch for as we FINALLY end the preseason.

Will the Lakers get a more complete look?

Luka Dončić was a full participant in Thursday's practice after sitting out Tuesday's game in Las Vegas. If he plays Friday, watch how the offense operates with Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler finally all on the floor together.

Kessler's screening and movement toward the basket should give both guards another option, while their ability to draw defenders can create opportunities for him around the rim. Getting those reads and chemistry right requires possessions together.

Collin Sexton went without the kinesiology tape on his right leg at Friday's shootaround after wearing it Thursday. Maybe we see him make his Lakers debut on Friday.

Ziaire Williams also practiced fully Thursday, saying the swelling in his left foot had subsided and he "felt great." His potential return would give Redick another wing to evaluate alongside the main group.

Adou Thiero was limited Thursday for what Redick described as "just maintenance." Cameron Carr did not practice, and the Lakers had not disclosed why he was unavailable in Las Vegas or Thursday, though he remained with the team.

Any final clues about the starting lineup?

The two starting spots alongside Dončić, Reaves and Kessler remain a storyline entering the finale.

Even Quentin Grimes, who has started every preseason game, offered no answers when asked whether anyone on the team knew who would fill them.

"I don't know. I guess you're going to find out next Wednesday," Grimes said.

He described the process as creating "healthy competition" throughout camp. Friday provides one more opportunity for players to make their case.

Watch which combinations Redick uses with his three established starters, particularly if more wings are available. The opening lineup will draw attention, but the substitutions could offer just as much insight into which players fit together.

Spacing, defensive assignments and the ability to contribute without needing the ball should all matter in those decisions.

The Lakers have been outrebounded in three of their four preseason games while allowing an average of 14.8 offensive rebounds in those games. The most was 20 against the Kings last Thursday.

This prompted Redick to devote practice time to the issue. L.A. went through "three different box-out drills" Thursday.

Friday offers a chance to see whether that work produces better habits.

Watch what happens when a shot goes up: whether defenders find a body, whether guards help collect rebounds and whether the Lakers finish possessions after forcing misses.

Kessler can help protect the basket, but securing the rebound requires everyone to stay involved. That is one area where the Lakers can show progress regardless of who is available.

articles.title: Alamo Heights quarterback Easton Stone voted Express-News Athlete of the Week
articles.summary: The senior threw for 276 yards and four touchdowns on 15-of-21 passing in a 63-31 victory over fellow Class 5A power Liberty Hill.
articles.body:
With Alamo Heights looking to stay in the hunt for a District 13-5A-II title and facing a showdown with another Class 5A power, Liberty Hill, quarterback Easton Stone answered the call.

The senior led the Mules' potent offense to perfection in a 63-31 victory over the Panthers, and now he has been voted Express-News Athlete of the Week.

Stone completed 15 of 21 passes for 276 yards and four touchdowns against Liberty Hill, continuing a strong senior campaign. The win moved Alamo Heights (6-1, 2-1) into a tie for second with Liberty Hill and Liberty Hill Legacy Ranch, just one loss behind undefeated Boerne. The Mules lost a heartbreaker to the Greyhounds, 38-31, in the district opener.

Stone beat out four fellow finalists in the Athlete of the Week poll.

Devine junior Enoch Hall was the engine for the Warhorses against Poteet, averaging 14.5 yards per carry. He finished with 160 rushing yards and five touchdowns in the 47-6 win over the Aggies, earning Offensive Player of the Week honors.

The Defensive Player of the Week, Brandeis junior Ah'maury Hamilton, recorded a team-high 19 tackles in a vital 33-29 win over Churchill. The victory was the Broncos' first 28-6A win of the season and helped them stay in the playoff picture.

Alamo Heights sophomore Mia Moshier was named Volleyball Player of the Week after she combined for 41 kills in a pair of wins over McCollum and Jay. She stuffed the stat sheet against the Cowboys, notching 25 kills, 19 digs and four blocks in a four-set victory.

San Antonio Christian junior Sara Cleveland combined for 44 kills, 11 blocks and 31 digs across three matches as the Lions beat Laredo St. Augustine, St. Anthony and Brownsville St. Joseph. She notched her 1,000th career kill against St. Joseph.

articles.title: Five Key Visits to Track Out West This Weekend
articles.summary: We track the five most significant visits being taken by Western recruits this weekend...
articles.body:
There are several key games taking place this weekend, with Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC schools hosting key games.

But here, we track the five most significant visits being taken by Western recruits this weekend.

4-star 2028 OT Aden Owolabi visiting Oklahoma

Dru Samia once went from Danville (Calif.) San Ramon Valley to Norman and the Sooners would love to have lightning strike twice with Owolabi, the No. 1 prospect in California in the 2028 class, visiting this weekend when the Sooners host Kentucky. They've been on his extreme short list from the jump and he's well aware of Samia's history with the Sooners, where he was a four-year starter and All-American and Owolabi is even better at the same stage.

4-star 2028 LB Landon Miller visiting UCLA

How much positive momentum has UCLA built with a 5-0 start under Bob Chesney? Miller didn't even have UCLA really on his radar pre-season, and had no plans to take a visit to Pasadena to watch them play. He was at USC two weeks ago, already making one trip to the Southland but then last weekend, took a visit to Oregon and saw the Bruins win in Eugene. That quickly led to the Concord (Calif.) De La Salle linebacker setting up an unofficial visit to UCLA, who never backed down despite having little traction and they're now very much in the race for him.

4-star 2028 QB Titus Huard visiting Kansas State

Kansas State has been in the top echelon of schools for Huard for quite some time. The Highlands Ranch (Colo.) Valor Christian quarterback was in Manhattan last month, but this time, he's bringing the whole family, including his father, Brock, a former NFL quarterback. It's clear that Collin Klein has prioritized Huard, who like Klein, is from Colorado and now getting a second visit, including the family, only enhances their chances with him.

4-star 2028 WR Quincey Clay visiting Oregon

Since Dan Lanning took over at Oregon, the Ducks have had major success in Idaho- Kenyon Sadiq , Gatlin Bair and then last year, Hudson Lewis , have been their success stories. Clay was at the USC-Oregon game in Los Angeles, but instead of USC offering him after the game, the Ducks did instead and now he's planning to visit this weekend for the game with Nebraska and Oregon has been a longtime dream school for him. Like Sadiq, Bair and Lewis, Clay played for RARE 7v7 in Idaho so the Ducks would like to keep that going with the Boise (Idaho) Capital receiver.

4-star 2028 DB Jaelyn Easterling-Flores visiting Oklahoma

Oklahoma already has a commitment from Goodyear (Ariz.) Desert Edge in 2027 cornerback Mikyal Davis . But they'd love to make it consecutive years with Scorpions and they're in the final six for the four-star safety, a Top 100 player nationally and a Navy All-American Bowl selection. The Sooners have been making a big push for him and Davis has been recruiting him to Norman as well and he's another headliner set to visit this weekend.

articles.title: 49ers vs. Commanders Preview: San Francisco Looks to Stay Undefeated
articles.summary: 49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washin...
articles.body:
49ers Aim to Keep Rolling on Monday Night

The San Francisco 49ers return home Monday night looking to extend their undefeated start when they host the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants.

The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC.

Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense

Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments.

Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success.

Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo.

The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult.

Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington

Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly.

Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie.

Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs.

Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities.

The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away.

For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage.

articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reported Internal Outlook Regarding Gunther's Booking

Recasting Street Fighter with WWE Stars 🎬

Some in WWE have reportedly been questioning the recent booking direction of two-time world heavyweight champion Gunther.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ), there is "a mild sense of frustration and confusion" over how Gunther has been utilized on SmackDown over the past few weeks.

One source told WrestleVotes that some people in creative have questioned whether The Ring General is being used properly when taking into consideration what he accomplished in 2025 and early in 2026.

On the heels of retiring Goldberg, John Cena and AJ Styles, Gunther heavily pursued the WWE Championship, but he has fallen short in numerous opportunities to win it.

That included a loss to Cody Rhodes at Clash in Italy, and a loss in a Triple Threat match for the WWE title against Rhodes and Sami Zayn at Night of Champions.

Gunther did bounce back to beat SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis at SummerSlam, but he subsequently lost a WWE Championship No. 1 contender's match, and later lost a Money in the Bank ladder match qualifying match.

Amid his recent cold streak, Gunther had been interacting backstage with Danhausen, leading to several instances of The Ring General intimidating him.

Gunther and Danhausen were scheduled to have a match last week, but instead, Gunther decimated Danhausen before the bell even rang.

It has been a strange spot for a serious wrestler like Gunther since Danhausen is one of the preeminent comedic wrestlers in the business.

While it may only prove to be a blip on the radar before Gunther moves on to bigger and better things, Gunther's current position is undoubtedly a bit of a surprise based on how he has been booked and presented for the entirety of his main roster run.

WWE Reportedly Planning Reigns vs. Femi, More for WrestleMania 43

WrestleMania 43 is still about six months away, but WWE reportedly already has a good idea of some of the major matches it wants to headline the show.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t WrestlePurists ), WWE has discussed Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi and CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes for the event. The company reportedly also wants to heavily feature Rhea Ripley provided she is cleared from the knee injury she is currently working her way back from.

WrestleVotes noted that while the aforementioned matches and plans have been proposed and talked about, they are not yet set in stone.

The Reigns vs. Femi idea comes as little surprise, as many have assumed it would be the WrestleMania 43 main event dating back to WrestleMania 42.

Femi beat Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, while Reigns won the World Heavyweight Championship from Punk. After the show, The Ruler called out Reigns.

Oba won King of the Ring and could have challenged Reigns, but he decided to conclude his rivalry with Lesnar first instead, and it was clear at that point that WWE was kicking the proverbial can down the road as it relates to Oba and Roman.

Punk and Rhodes faced off at SummerSlam with Punk beating Rhodes to retain the WWE Championship, but there has yet to be a rematch.

While neither Punk nor Rhodes hold a title right now, it won't be at all surprising if one of them wins back the WWE Championship before WrestleMania 43 to set up another clash between them.

As for Ripley, she has been on the shelf since early June due to a torn meniscus that required surgery.

Assuming Ripley is back in time to build toward a meaningful match at WrestleMania, there is little doubt that she will be put in that spot given her long history of significant WrestleMania matches against the likes of Charlotte Flair, Becky Lynch, Bianca Belair, Iyo Sky and other big names.

The ankle injury Stephanie Vaquer was nursing during Monday night's episode of Raw was reportedly not part of a storyline.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), Vaquer got legitimately injured at Money in the Bank, although it is not expected to keep her out of action for long.

At Money in the Bank, Vaquer attempted to defend the Women's World Championship against Liv Morgan and Becky Lynch in a Triple Threat match, but Morgan hit her with Oblivion to pin her and win back the women's world title.

On the subsequent episode of Raw, Vaquer was seen backstage on crutches, but she said she would be back in action soon and even teased an eventual singles match against Lynch.

La Primera previously missed an extended period of time when she was injured around the time of WrestleMania 42.

She was off WWE programming for more than three months before returning in August and targeting Morgan, who beat her for the Women's World Championship at WrestleMania.

Vaquer won the title back from Morgan at a live event in her home country of Chile last month, but she dropped it back to Liv about a month later at Money in the Bank.

Now, Vaquer is fighting through another injury, but every indication is that she won't be on the shelf for long this time.

articles.title: Real Madrid Magic And Drama In Manchester: What Stood Out With Europe's Top Clubs
articles.summary: Who really suffers in the Manchester City controversy? And what's going at Real Madrid, Inter Milan and Manchester United?
articles.body: "When kings fall, they fall on top of us." Those are the words of one of my favorite writers, the Jamaican author Marlon James, as he poignantly says in his fantasy novel Black Leopard, Red Wolf.There is something so delicate about an empire. Its longevity very much depends on not just the health of the institution but of the stakeholders who make the decisions. And as we take a look around the world of global football, you can’t find a truer phrase when discussing Manchester City, which has become one of the biggest talking points in sports right now. But plenty of other top clubs are making news, so let's dive into what's sticking out. Click on a team to navigate this post. Man City Fans Are Caught In Tough Spot ... There is such a current alienated experience when discussing Manchester City because nothing that happens on the pitch for Enzo Maresca’s side will escape the gray cloud that hovers over the Etihad. I am, of course, talking about the verdict that was handed to them last month when an independent commission found Man City guilty of the vast majority of 115 charges for breaching the Premier League’s financial rules. The most damning of them being the creation of "sham" contracts, which were hidden funds through their own ownership (Abu Dhabi United Group) thus inflating revenue by more than a billion dollars over the course of 10 years. City basically invented external revenue and in the Premier League and European football, where the pyramid of club hierarchy is the core foundation of the game. When an owner does something like this and it doesn’t get regulated, it becomes a slippery slope for everyone else. Teams will take advantage of its own expenditure against everyone else, who may not have the means of a state-owned club. This is a devastating but just outcome for City, one the club is appealing, which means the people, the fans, both inside and outside of the club, will have to wait until the beginning of 2027 to hear the punishment. But a punishment must be given because this is a historic breach that has shaken the game. And as I said, when the power crumbles, it is not the mighty who truly suffer, it is the community and until Man City deal with the consequences, Premier League fans of other clubs will treat them as villains, and rightly so. It will be the football equivalent of Cersei’s shameful walk of atonement in Game of Thrones where we, the people, scream ‘Shame!’ every time they touch the ball. ...And A Loss To Mighty PSG Didn't Help That’s what you saw last weekend as City, quite happily playing the role of a theater villain, won convincingly 3-0 at Liverpool. As City fans celebrated after the final whistle, Anfield’s DJ played Fleetwood Mac’s "Little Lies," which was the perfect way to describe the current state of things in the Premier League. But this week in the UEFA Champions League, back at their stadium, in front of Pep Guardiola who was sitting behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano, City suffered a 4-2 loss to the mighty PSG (also state owned who has dealt with similar breaches with UEFA in the past) in a performance that quite literally shook them. Luis Enrique’s defending champions were incredible, especially in the first half and City simply couldn’t escape the wrath of the French giants as the brilliant Desire Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Vitinha scored in the space of 19 minutes. City improved in the second half thanks to striker Erling Haaland’s brace, thus becoming the club’s highest goalscorer in the competition with 60 goals in 60 career appearances. No player has ever done that at such an age and at that pace. But in the end, it was the defending champion PSG who outclassed its opponent. So what’s next? City host Ipswich Town this Saturday in what should be a better result (though the newly promoted side is showing some fight and currently in 10th place) but the gray cloud will continue to drift above the Etihad and it won’t end until we learn of the punishment. But as I said, don’t hold your breath. ↑ Return To Top Man Utd's Martinez Said The Quiet Part Out Loud On the west side of Manchester, Manchester United lost to Atlético de Madrid this week in the Champions League in what was once again a flat, naive performance from the Red Devils. Michael Carrick’s side is now winless in its last five matches and the latest loss against Atletico Madrid gave us an interview from defender Lisandro Martínez for the ages where the Argentinian defender criticized the direction of the club, specifically highlighting the issues with the hierarchy. "…I expect more [investment]. 100%," said Martínez, speaking to Amazon Prime in the UK during his post-game interview. "I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox]. I have to be honest, as players we have to do more, but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night." Some pockets of the media think this was a monologue spoken in the wrong environment, including club legend Wayne Rooney, whilst others want him to suffer more consequences than simply a fine. But to me, this was a refreshing piece of honesty from a player who is entering his final year of his contract, knowing too well he is not staying. And just like Jerry Maguire’s mission statement, he spoke out on what needed to change within a powerful institution. And he’s right. United, at this point, are not equipped to deal with both domestic and Champions League football against strong opponents and a lot of that has to do with executive decision-making that failed to bring the right personnel this summer. There is not enough cover at the left-back role and the No. 9 position remains in desperate need for a 20+ goal scorer. The midfield is also in question. Problems continue for a club who has a manager entering, for the first time ever as a head coach, a season where he has to handle domestic and European football. But just like Jerry — as he dramatically left the agency with a goldfish and Renée Zellweger’s Dorothy Boyd - Martínez will also say goodbye to Man United at some point when in reality, many fans wish it was the ownership. There’s a massive match coming up this weekend against Leeds United at Elland Road and if the Red Devils lose and do it badly, the temperature at United will rise and Carrick’s future might just be in peril. ↑ Return To Top Real Madrid Always Comes Back To Haunt You Let’s discuss another giant of European football in Real Madrid. Its incredible 4-3 comeback against Roma at the Olimpico was a testament of Madrid’s undying reputation. In the spirit of October, Kylian Mbappé and Co. are the football equivalent of Halloween’s Michael Myers. No matter how many times you may think you have escaped or overcome the adversary, it will always come back to haunt you. You simply cannot kill it. And that’s Real Madrid, even this version, which is still trying to figure itself out under manager Jose Mourinho. The issue for the Spanish giant is that there is quite a distance between Los Blancos and Barcelona and the special one has to find a way to help the most valuable club in the world find its identity. It doesn’t help when you have a chaotic midfield and a star like Vinícius Júnior, who continues to give subpar performances. He is also now suspended for pulling an opponent’s hair in the previous domestic match, thus missing four matches, one of them being El Clásico on October 25th. But this might be a blessing in disguise because Vini’s absence might just allow Real Madrid to breathe a little better going forward and prioritize the truly important area: midfield. All I know is that Mourinho has to figure out Madrid’s consistency sooner rather than later because, in the end, Jamie Lee Curtis did overcome Michael Myers. Madrid can possibly fall deeper and create an even larger gap between themselves and Barcelona – who, alongside PSG, is currently the best team in Europe. ↑ Return To Top Who Is Stopping Inter Milan? Mainly Themselves Allow me to talk about Internazionale for a moment. The Italian defending champions lost 4-3 to Club Brugge in the Champions League this week and despite leading Serie A, things are very tight at the top as the club has an advantage only on goal difference over Lazio. Roma is also creeping behind by only two points and Cagliari by three. If there are any more mishaps for the Nerazzurri it could see Cristian Chivu’s team lose its advantage at the top. What’s made matters worse is that its legendary striker and leader Lautaro Martínez — who scored a brace against Brugge and is the team’s top scorer — suffered a hamstring injury after the match and will sadly miss a significant amount of time, including the Milan derby on October 31st, which is of course, Halloween. And to that point, allow me to use another fun analogy. If Inter was a horror movie character, who would it be? At this very moment, it is undoubtedly the costumed serial killer from Wes Craven’s slasher classic from 1996, Scream, specifically the scene when he is chasing a screaming Drew Barrymore. We know how dangerous it is, we know the threat and the terror of the masked character as they run up the stairs chasing the desperate victim — but at every given opportunity to attack and finish the job, they just continue to trip. And that’s Inter. It is a threatening opponent with much to worry about, but for some reason, at this moment and as we saw in the Champions League, the Italian giants continue to stumble due to their own undoing. ↑ Return To Top

articles.title: Cardinals' rookie RB Jeremiyah Love ruled out vs. Rams with lingering ankle injury
articles.summary: (AP) — Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love won't play for the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams because of a lingering left ankle injur...
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Rookie running back Jeremiyah Love won't play for the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday against the Los Angeles Rams because of a lingering left ankle injury.

The No. 3 overall pick out of Notre Dame hasn't practiced all week and was ruled out on the team's injury report released on Friday.

"There's no discussion of IR or anything like that," first-year coach Mike LaFleur said. "We've got to re-evaluate, really every single day. Not good enough obviously right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him."

Love has been a big part of the Cardinals' offense through the first five weeks with a team-high 245 yards rushing and a touchdown. He's also caught 11 passes for 36 yards and a TD.

"He's doing good, but you guys see the way he cuts, just being candid, he cuts hard, that's a superpower of his," LaFleur said. "And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right right now."

The Cardinals (1-4) enter Sunday's game against the Rams (2-3) on a four-game losing streak and have lost eight straight games against NFC West opponents.

articles.title: John Lynch: George Kittle asked me if we're trying to trade for Khalil Mack
articles.summary: The trade deadline was a topic of conversation for General Manager John Lynch on Friday.
articles.body:
The trade deadline was a topic of conversation for General Manager John Lynch on Friday.

Lynch was a guest on KNBR and he was asked if calls are picking up with the November 10 deadline drawing closer. Lynch said that the calls have picked up of late and that the team has made its own "just to kind of see where the market's at" right now.

Lynch was also asked specifically about interest in Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack.

"I can't tell you that ," Lynch said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "A lot of people ask me that. We seem to be connected to everyone, and I don't know where that comes from. I had a player ask me that yesterday."

Lynch eventually named tight end George Kittle as the inquisitive player, which isn't surprising "because he asks about everything." Kittle's interest in the prospect makes sense, however. The 49ers are 5-0 and should feel good enough about their chances to make a run that they'd be willing to bolster the roster ahead of the deadline. On the other hand, the Chargers are 0-5 and should be considering picking up assets for the future with this season headed off the rails.

articles.summary: After a trade with the Utah Jazz, former Notre Dame forward Kelly Tripucka spent three seasons with the Charlotte Hornets.
articles.body:
In one of the best trades in Hornets franchise history, Charlotte traded center Mike Brown to the Utah Jazz ahead of the 1988-89 season in exchange for former No. 12 overall pick Kelly Tripucka. After averaging 7.5 points with Utah during the 1987-88 season, Tripucka averaged 22.6 points in his first season with the Hornets, more than a 15-point increase.

The former Notre Dame forward would go on to play three seasons with the Hornets before playing professionally in France. In 227 appearances with Charlotte, Tripucka averaged 14.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 0.9 steals and 0.2 blocks while shooting 45.1% from the field and 35.6% from 3-point range. Throughout his 10-year career between the Hornets, Jazz and Pistons, Tripucka averaged 17.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, three assists and one steal.

articles.body:
After the exodus commenced upon the conclusion of last season, Macy Comito reaffirmed her commitment to Iowa State.

Comito originally made her commitment to the Cyclones in August of 2024, and officially signed on Nov. 12, 2025. Even if the roster is a little different (nine transfers out and eight coming in is normal, right?) Comito has been in the blueprint for a long time. Bill described her as "born to be a cyclone" as both of her parents attended Iowa State.

Macy Comito has an incredibly decorated resume at the high school level. From Carlisle, Iowa, Comito holds school records in:

Pretty good. She also earned 4A All-State honors three times, First-Team All-Iowa twice, was named All-Conference for all four years of high school, and set a Class 4A record with 42 points in one state tournament game. In the 2025-26 season, she led Carlisle to a state championship victory and was named the 2026 Iowa Class 4A Player of the Year as well as All-Tournament team captain.

Naturally, she also received a 2026 Academic All-State selection and was named to the Academic All-Conference four times, so it is safe to say that she has amassed success both on and off the court.

One of many guards on the new roster, Comito will still have to work to stand out among a roster that is bringing a lot of collegiate experience, albeit primarily from other programs. Still, her quickness, three point prowess, and defensive ability will certainly be utilized throughout the season. A court with Comito, Arriana Jackson, and Evangelia Paulk could be one of the best defensive trios in the Big-12. Iowa State averaged just 5.72 steals per game during conference play last season, which ranked 15th in the conference.

On the offensive side, Bill Fennelly has been outspoken recently about returning to the "Iowa State Way". Any longtime fan reads that and knows that the three pointers are going to be aplenty. "I don't know what the biggest green light there is, but they all have it," Fennelly stated in a recent press conference. That should be music to Comito's ears, as she will have plenty of opportunities to find open teammates beyond the arc as well as finding her own opportunities to pull the trigger from deep. A faster, more dynamic offense may also clear some more driving lanes for the offense, so it will be key to see how Comito maximises the speed and range potential of this offense as one of the point guards.

If you want to buy early in a cyclone of the future, Comito is one of the best bets you can make. Iowa State has been with Comito for her entire life, and if she can translate the success that she experienced at Carlisle over to the collegiate level? You better watch out.

articles.title: Washington Football Second-Year WR Beacon of Light on Bleak Offense
articles.summary: Despite not producing as many touchdowns as Washington has needed through the first half of 2026, Dezmen Roebuck has been the go-to guy so far.
articles.body:
Washington Huskies second-year wide receiver Dezmen Roebuck has statistically been one of the best in the country through the first half of the 2026 college football season.

The 5-foot-11, 190-pound pass catcher is No. 6 in the FBS with 286 yards after catch and No. 5 in receptions (43) going into the Huskies ' second Big Ten road game this Friday at Purdue. Although the Marana, Arizona native has just 387 receiving yards, tied for No. 59 in the country and just seven more yards than his classmate and teammate Chris Lawson, there is more to Roebuck than that.

"It's Dez," wide receivers coach Kevin Cummings responded Tuesday when asked about the most physical run blocker in his room. "Yeah, it's Dez. It was fun watching him the other night he had a battle with Iowa's nickel (Jacob Wallace). They were getting after it. That was fun to watch."

Roebuck was one of three receivers to haul in a touchdown from backup quarterback Elijah Brown in the Huskies' 41-24 loss to the Hawkeyes at Husky Stadium last Friday. Late in the third quarter, the UW slot receiver broke free just enough from fifth-year Iowa defensive back Deshaun Lee to cut the deficit to 34-18 following a two-point conversion.

Through his first six games as a freshman in 2025, Roebuck had nearly the same receiving yards (318) and an equal number of touchdowns (2). However, as expected with the departures of veterans Denzel Boston and Omari Evans, Roebuck has more than doubled his receptions total from 18 to 43, and that held true when Brown came in for the injured Demond Williams Jr. in the second half.

Jedd Fisch and the Huskies' offense will need Roebuck to continue to produce as the unit searching for a significant improvement against the Boilermakers. Through three conference games against Illinois, Minnesota and UCLA, fourth-year coach Barry Odom's Purdue defense has only had one opposing receiver compile a 100-yard receiving game, Illini veteran Collin Dixon, who put up 10 receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown in a 24-17 loss two weeks ago.

Roebuck doesn't need to have his first 100-yard game in conference play—he's the only UW receiver to have a 100-yard game this season (121 yards vs Eastern Washington), with second-year tight end Baron Naone (103 yards) being the other, also against the Eagles—for the Huskies to return from West Lafayette with the first victory in league play.

He does, however, need to continue to produce as he has for Fisch and the offense to have at least a chance to overcome the Boilermakers at Ross–Ade Stadium.

articles.body: El nivel y competitividad del pádel femenino crece torneo a torneo, el P1 de Milano acoge en la jornada de sábado a las cuatros mejores parejas del mundo por tercer torneo consecutivo Gemma Triay y Delfi Brea quieren reivindicarse en las semifinales del torneo en Italia, la pareja uno femenina ha avanzado a esta ronda tras vencer sin problemas a la única pareja fuera del top-8 femenina en cuartos. Impusieron su ritmo desde el principio Triay y Brea colocando con rapidez el 6-2 en el marcador, pero Velasco y Eugenio se reengancharon en el segundo asalto hasta forzar el tie-break momento en el que la veteranía y madurez de las chicas de Seba Nerone se impusieron (7-6). Sus rivales en la jornada de sábado serán Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero, al igual que en los otros dos torneos de esta gira europea de Premier Padel. Las catalanas se volvían a medir en cuartos de final a Osoro y Salazar como en su último torneo y aunque estuvo más competido esta vez, la pareja tres no dio opción en ningún momento a las chicas de Martín Canali con un contundente 6-4/ 6-3. Bea González y Paula Josemaría sellaron su pase a semifinales después de que Tamara Icardo y Claudia Jensen se vieran obligadas a abandonar el encuentro. Las número dos se adjudicaron el primer set por un contundente 6-1, pero Icardo, que regresaba a la competición en Milán tras su lesión, optó por retirarse al comprobar que aún no estaba al cien por cien para afrontar la exigencia de un partido de este nivel. La valenciana priorizó su recuperación para evitar riesgos y poder regresar en plenas condiciones en el próximo torneo. Una vuelta a la competición que tendrá que esperar un poco más, mientras González y Josemaría vuelven a unas semifinales. En el último turno de la jornada, Claudia Fernández y Martina Calvo confirmaron que el título conquistado en Düsseldorf no fue fruto de un momento aislado. Las campeonas se impusieron por 6-1 y 6-2 a Marta Ortega y Sofía Araújo, dominando el encuentro desde el inicio y sin dar margen a sus rivales para meterse en la pelea. La pareja número cuatro mantiene así la inercia ganadora con la que aterrizó en Milán y vuelve a instalarse en unas semifinales, donde les espera precisamente el reto de medirse, una vez más, a Bea González y Paula Josemaría.

articles.title: Leeds vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, prediction, lineups
articles.summary: Manchester United are mired in poor form – and Lisandro Martinez’s meltdown – now they face on-the-up rivals Leeds.
articles.body:
Who: Leeds United vs Manchester United What: English Premier League Where: Elland Road, Leeds, United Kingdom When: Sunday, October 18, at 2pm local time (13:00 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 9:00 GMT ahead of our live text commentary stream

Manchester United against Leeds United has long been one of the fiercest rivalries in football.

The former’s closest shot to ending their wait since 1967 for an English top flight title came in 1993 when Sir Alex Ferguson’s side were pipped to the title by the latter.

The following year United’s wait was over as Ferguson’s side – buoyed by the arrival of Eric Cantona from Leeds – lifted the inaugural Premier League crown.

The rest for United and Ferguson was history, but since the most successful manager in English football retired the Old Trafford club have been in decline.

The fortunes of Leeds, who have won three league titles, dipped dramatically after that last piece of domestic silverware. Ten years later, they were relegated and three years were even spent in League One, the third tier of English football.

Now the Elland Road club are back in the top flight, having won the Championship two seasons ago, and have an eye on the top four this weekend.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at the match that for Leeds marks the arrival of their fiercest rivals, who have lurched to a 40-year low.

How have Leeds United fared this season?

Leeds have lost only one of their six league games this season, a 2-1 reverse at Arsenal in their last match when the Premier League holders were second best for much of the match and were forced to come from behind.

Two wins and two draws in their first five league matches saw Leeds holding onto the coat-tails of Arsenal and City.

That run culminated with a stunning 4-1 home win against Newcastle United.

A disappointing home draw with Crystal Palace sat in between the defeat at Arsenal .

A 6-3 defeat at Chelsea ended their League Cup hopes, but the home side needed two goals in the last ten minutes to pull clear in the thrilling encounter.

How have Manchester United fared this season?

United’s season – and Michael Carrick’s start as permanent manager – couldn’t have got off to a worse start with a 2-0 defeat at newly-promoted Hull City.

When the Red Devils fell a goal behind against another promoted side, Ipswich Town, at Old Trafford in their next match, the warning signs were there.

Carrick’s side came back to win 5-2 – and that remains United’s only league win of the season.

A contentious 1-0 home defeat by Manchester City – in which a controversial VAR decision separated the sides – has been one of United’s better performances with deflating draws against Everton , Fulham and Tottenham surrounding the derby.

United were also dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton, who overcame the home side’s early 2-0 first-half lead to the disbelief of Old Trafford.

What is the latest on Lisandro Martinez’s Manchester United criticism?

Defender Lisandro ‌‌Martinez will be available for Sunday’s game after ⁠⁠United accepted ⁠⁠his apology for criticising its transfer policy, Carrick told reporters on Friday.

Martinez met Carrick and senior club officials on Thursday, two days after suggesting United ⁠⁠needed greater investment to compete at the highest level following their 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid.

The centre back later apologised for his remarks and Carrick ⁠⁠sought to downplay the episode when he spoke to reporters on Friday.

“We’ve moved on from that. It was one of those things. It’s really not a drama for the group,” Carrick said.

“The squad have trained really well and they are in good spirits. There is ‌‌a freshness about the group…

What happened the last time Leeds played Manchester United?

Leeds were 2-1 winners at Old Trafford when the sides met in the Premier League in April.

Noah Okafor scored both goals for Leeds to inflict the only defeat of Carrick’s interim tenure, having replaced Ruben Amorim as manager.

Martinez was sent off early in the second half, but Casemiro offered United some hope just after the hour mark.

En la jornada de cuartos se volvían a ver las caras con Guerrero-Leal tras el P1 de Pretoria y la revancha de los Golden Boys ha estado a la altura de lo esperado, doble 6-2 y desquiciando por momentos a la joven pareja española. Y quien les espera en las semifinales es la pareja que ha intentado arrebatarles los sus dos últimos títulos, Stupaczuk y Sanz. La pareja cuatro tiene novedades en el banquillo, ya que es la primera vez que Carlos Pozzoni les dirige fuera de la pista, no obstante eso no les ha hecho bajar el nivel. En cuartos han eliminado a Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo con un resultado de 6-3 en un primer set que han controlado sin problemas, la segunda manga ha mantenido la misma tónica cerrando el partido por 6-4. Fede Chingotto y Ale Galán quieren reencontrarse con los títulos y el tercer paso en el Milano P1 era duro, Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso. Los de Martínez, conocedores del gran nivel que venía desplegando esta pareja, entró al partido con la ambición que acostumbran para llevarse el primer set por un contundente 6-3 aprovechando todas sus ocasiones. Pero Libaak y Alfonso no habían dicho aún la última palabra. El segundo set parecía encarrilado cuando Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto encontraron el break en el quinto juego para tomar ventaja por 4-2. La pareja número dos tenía el partido donde quería, pero entonces emergió un descomunal Gonza Alfonso, dispuesto a convertir cada pelota en una oportunidad para el espectáculo. El argentino desató una colección de golpes imposibles sobre el 20x10, devolvió el break y llevó de nuevo la igualdad al marcador. La pareja número 15 tuvo en sus manos la posibilidad de forzar el tercer set, pero dejó escapar hasta tres pelotas que terminaron pesando como una losa. En el ‘tie break’, Galán y Chingotto no perdonaron y cerraron el encuentro por 6-3 y 7-6, sobreviviendo a la rebelión de unos rivales que estuvieron a punto de prolongar la batalla. Los últimos en conseguir su billete a las semifinales fueron Lebrón y Augsburger que aguantaron el buen nivel de Garrido y De Pascual en su inicio como pareja. El primer set fue un intercambio de golpes que se resolvió en el tie-break en favor de los chicos de Silingo con un contundente 7-1 en el marcador. Ese bajón tras terminar el primer set lo acusaron Javi y Juani, que sufrieron un quiebre nada más comenzar el segundo set, distancia que se mantuvo hasta el final del set por 6-3.

articles.body:
We're still dealing with the fallout from the Money in the Bank PLE, but as of now, WWE is still preparing for Crown Jewel on November 7.

Here's a look at what WWE advertised for Friday's show:

Rey Fenix vs. Ricky Saints (AAA Cruiserweight Championship)

Let's take a look at everything that happened on this week's SmackDown.

This week's show opened with Sami Zayn coming out with Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae. Zayn began by asking the crowd who came to be ride or die for the last real good guy. The crowd did not seem to react much.

He said Penta should probably focus on Reigns with his Money in the Bank briefcase before Trick Williams' music interrupted him. The United States champion said every time Zayn sees him, he is reminded of how the crowd turned on him.

Zayn told him that he headbutted Williams the last time they saw each other because he was trying to teach him something, not disrespect him. He told Trick he doesn't have what it takes to be the WWE champion.

Trick dared him to take a swing, but before anything could happen, Gargano grabbed the mic and yelled at Williams. This led to Williams calling for a ref to kick off the first match of the night.

This is one of those segments that tried to stretch something simple out for way too long. This could have been wrapped up in five minutes. Everyone did their job, but there is only so much you can do when you have very little material.

The match between Williams and Gargano was already underway by the time the show returned from a break.

They traded a few counters before Williams began favoring his knee following a bad landing from a leap frog. Johnny Wrestling noticed and started going after the knee, but Trick didn't let him have control for too long.

The match was relatively tame until Williams turned up the intensity at ringside by slamming Gargano's head into the announce table a few times. From that point forward, things felt much more competitive.

Williams is a rising star, and Gargano is a celebrated veteran, and since this isn't a combo that has been done to death, this was a solid way to kick off the action on the show. Both guys looked good, but it definitely took them a little time to find their groove with each other.

Johnny Wrestling put up a great fight, but Williams hit the Book End for the win.

Lil Yachty was not with Williams this week.

Vic Joseph sucked up to Zayn a little on commentary.

If you look at the way Williams works now and how he was when he first got to the main roster, you can see a clear difference. He knows when to do certain things to pop the crowd better than he used to.

Trick's delayed vertical suplex was nice.

If the Browns are able to win this game, they will be back in first place in the division, which would be incredible considering how low expectations were for their season.

Former Cleveland Browns quarterback Tyler Huntley will get the start this week, and though he got a win last week, he isn't anywhere near the threat that Jackson is.

The Browns have done a good job pressuring opposing quarterbacks, but with Jackson out there will be a lot of emphasis on trying to slow down Derek Henry. articles.title: Kyle Shanahan heaps praise on Commanders QB Jayden Daniels
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan loves what he's seen from Jayden Daniels this season.
articles.body:
Head coach Kyle Shanahan has seen enough film of Jayden Daniels to know what the San Francisco 49ers are up against Monday night.

Shanahan praised the Commanders quarterback Thursday, both for his throwing prowess and his ability to run the ball.

"Since he came in the league until now, Jayden's got a chance to be one of the better quarterbacks in this league without a doubt," Shanahan said. "If you take away the running element of him, just how he plays in the pocket is so natural with how accurate he is, how strong his arm is, how poised he is going through a progression, how fearless he is hanging in there and taking a hit, keeping his eyes down the field.

"He's got the speed and the coordination to win games only with his legs, which means you want to keep him in the pocket and not let him out because he can beat you with his legs. However, he's a very scary quarterback in the pocket just playing the position. So, he's got all the tools to be as good as there is."

Daniels' 2024 rookie season showed that. He threw for 3,568 yards with 25 touchdowns and nine interceptions, made the Pro Bowl and won Offensive Rookie of the Year. He started seven games in 2025 due to injuries, though, and only finished with 1,262 yards with eight touchdowns and three interceptions, while the Commanders went 2-5.

This season he's producing at a good rate despite still missing time with an elbow injury. Daniels has thrown for 459 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions in three games. Despite the Commanders' 1-3-1 record, Shanahan expects Washington to give the 49ers a run for their undefeated record.

"I know we've got a really good team coming in here who's as hungry as can be and I know it's going to be probably our biggest challenge so far," he said.

articles.title: Report: Florida expected to start Tramell Jones at Texas
articles.summary: Florida is expected to start Tramell Jones at quarterback against Texas as Aaron Philo works through a shoulder injury, per a report from On3.
articles.body:
Florida appears set to make a change at quarterback for Saturday's trip to Texas.

On3's Pete Nakos reported Friday that the Gators are expected to start Tramell Jones, with Aaron Philo continuing to work through a shoulder injury. Jones took first-team reps throughout the week while Philo was limited, although Nakos reported that a final decision will not be made until Saturday morning.

If Jones gets the nod, it would be his first college start.

The sophomore quarterback has appeared in five games this season, completing 23 of 29 passes for 252 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. His 79.3% completion rate has come mostly in second-half and reserve work.

Florida coach Jon Sumrall made it clear earlier this week that the staff has confidence in Jones if Philo is unavailable.

"Tramell got reps in practice. He's going to continue to get reps," Sumrall said. "I've said this publicly: I think Tramell can be our starting quarterback here, and we can win football games."

Philo has been listed as questionable on the SEC injury report this week and was already expected to be a game-time decision. The Georgia Tech transfer has passed for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions this season.

Jones chose to stay at Florida after Sumrall was hired rather than enter the transfer portal, and Sumrall has repeatedly praised how he has handled his role behind Philo.

"Tramell is gonna be ready when his number is called," Sumrall said. "I love the way he's handled himself. Tramell's been great. Philo's been great."

articles.body:
Jaylen Waddle hasn't had a pleasant start to his stint with the Denver Broncos . Besides one great game, the rest has been frustrating for fans to experience.

Waddle is going through the sixth season of his NFL career, his first with the Broncos. He spent the first five years with the Miami Dolphins before they traded him to Denver this past offseason.

Waddle hasn't begun the year promising. Aside from his Week 2 game where he caught eight passes for 138 yards, he hasn't replicated that form in the five other contests.

"#Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle was heavily featured in Week 2. Outside of that game… 5 games. 14 catches. 90 receiving yards. 1 TD. Long of 13 yards," reporter Ari Meirov wrote.

How Jaylen Waddle, Broncos played against Seahawks

Jaylen Waddle looks to get himself back on track to greatly help the Broncos offense. Despite this, they beat the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime on Thursday night.

It was mainly a defensive game between two sides as Denver led 14-3 at halftime. However, Seattle fought back by scoring 11 points in the fourth quarter to force overtime.The Seahawks had their chance to complete the comeback but were unable to get a score on their drive. This paved the way for Denver to get in the right position for Lutz to convert his 53-yard field goal to send the home crowd into a frenzy.

Bo Nix didn't have a performance to write home about as his struggles may put a cap on the team's ceiling. He only completed 17 out of 27 passes for 107 yards.

articles.summary: Recapping Friday's Cape Cod and Islands high school sports action.
articles.body:
Sandwich (10-2-0) completed the season sweep of Nauset (8-2-2) with a 3-1 victory on Friday in a Cape and Islands League Atlantic Division girls soccer matchup between two of the top teams in the region.

Lauren Meyer scored on either side of a goal by Gwen Reisig, including a free kick from the edge of the box.

Nauset failed to capitalize on some great early opportunities in the first half that would've given the Warriors the lead. Sandwich instead powered in front when Meyer scored on a long-range effort.

Reisig then made it 2-0 after sniffing out a second-chance ball on a corner kick following the restart.

Eloise MacMillan recorded Nauset's only goal after she was played in on goal by Caroline Bothfeld to pull within 2-1. She twisted and turned her way free of the last defender and slotted the ball into the bottom corner.

Meyer restored Sandwich's two-goal lead with 15 minutes to play when she turned in a free kick that went over the goalkeeper's head.

Nauset had strong play from Emi Valli, Chloe Burns and Bothfeld in the midfield, as well as from Evelyn Vaillancourt and Talia Nadeau on the wings.

Upper Cape 1, Wareham 0: The Rams (1-11-1) shook off their winless record in a nonleague matchup. They ended a five-match goalless drought in the process.

They were down 2-1 at halftime before Cam Lyons knotted things up on a breakaway pass from Mycah Hingston. Frank Greul then scored the winner on a header after he was set up by James Kirby's free kick. Ben Buckley tallied the first goal on an assist from Hingston. Maddy Campbell spread out the offense, dishing out 28 assists. Bella Magalhaes, Ava Johnston and Amalia Thompson recorded nine, eight and seven kills, respectively. The Red Hawks combined for 10 aces.

articles.title: Patriots Host 3 Running Backs for Tryouts Amid Injury Woes
articles.summary: The New England Patriots brought in three running backs for tryouts on Friday, one of whom is an old friend. The post Patriots Host 3 Running Backs for Tryou...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots have managed to get themselves back on track after an ugly start to the season thanks to a pair of big wins over the Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders. They aren't out of the woods yet, though, as injuries are continuing to pile up at an alarming rate.

One spot where New England has been short on depth from Week 1 is the running back spot, and it seems like the team is aware that it could use some more help here. As a result, the team decided to try out three free agent running backs on Friday in an effort to potentially reinforce its depth at this spot.

Patriots Tryout Ulysses Bentley, Terrell Jennings, and Josh Pitsenberger

Right now, the Pats have three running backs on their roster, but one of them (TreVeyon Henderson) is dealing with an ankle injury that could force him to miss the team's Week 6 action. That leaves just Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner, both of whom have had trouble with fumbling the football already this year.

We recently saw New England reunite with Hassan Haskins by signing him to the practice squad, and Lan Larison is also an option on the practice squad at this spot. In a move that could indicate Henderson is trending towards not playing on Sunday, though, the Pats brought in Ulysses Bentley, Terrell Jennings , and Josh Pitsenberger for tryouts on Friday.

Jennings is the name most Patriots fans will recognize, as he was the team's No. 3 running back last season after Antonio Gibson suffered a season-ending ACL injury in Week 5. Bentley has spent time with the Indianapolis Colts and New Orleans Saints , while Pitsenberger spent the summer with the Houston Texans after not getting selected in the 2026 NFL Draft.

"Patriots tried out three running backs: Ulysses Bentley, Terrell Jennings and Josh Pitsenberger," Adam Schefter of ESPN reported in a post on X.

Should the Patriots Sign Another Running Back?

The reunion with Haskins seemingly would have covered New England at this spot, but for whatever reason, it still seems to believe it needs more help at the running back position. Jennings is the most likely candidate to be signed, given his familiarity with the team, but the front office may simply be updating its list of potential running back targets in the event it needs to sign someone in the future.

If Henderson can't play on Sunday, look for the Pats to elevate either Larison or Haskins to the active roster for their upcoming game. New England will look to win its third straight game when it takes on the New York Jets in an important divisional clash, with kickoff for this contest scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

The Detroit Tigers are reportedly bringing a familiar face into the organization, and the move could have implications that go well beyond filling another coaching vacancy.

According to Friday's report on Detroit's coaching plans , the Tigers are expected to hire former Major League catcher Martin Maldonado as their new quality control coach, reuniting the 40-year-old with manager A.J. Hinch .

Maldonado spent 15 seasons in the big leagues, earned a Gold Glove Award, and helped the Houston Astros win the 2022 World Series. However, there's another connection that makes this addition particularly fascinating for Detroit.

Maldonado knows exactly what it's like to work with Tigers pitcher Framber Valdez.

And after Valdez's inconsistent first season in Detroit, that relationship could prove valuable.

Aug 19, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch (14) looks on during a seventh inning pitching change against the Pittsburgh Pirates at PNC Park. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Martin Maldonado Reunites With A.J. Hinch in Detroit

Maldonado and Hinch previously worked together with the Houston Astros during the 2018 and 2019 seasons. The veteran catcher developed a reputation for his game preparation, leadership, and ability to work with pitching staffs throughout his career.

After retiring following the 2025 season, Maldonado spent 2026 working as a special assistant with the Atlanta Braves. He will now have an opportunity to begin a new chapter in the dugout.

The reported addition fills an opening created when Billy Boyer moved from quality control coach to third-base coach following Joey Cora's departure in July.

Detroit still has additional coaching vacancies to address after parting ways with first-base coach Anthony Sanders and assistant pitching coach Juan Nieves.

As we previously examined during Detroit's offseason coaching overhaul , Hinch is making adjustments following a disappointing 76-86 campaign. Maldonado's arrival adds an experienced baseball mind to a staff looking for ways to help the Tigers return to contention.

But there's a reason this particular hire could be especially interesting.

The Framber Valdez Connection Could Be Significant

Maldonado spent several seasons catching Valdez in Houston, including during the Astros' 2022 World Series championship run.

In fact, Maldonado was behind the plate when Valdez pitched six outstanding innings against Philadelphia in the decisive Game 6 of the 2022 World Series. He also caught Valdez's no-hitter against Cleveland on August 1, 2023.

That is a significant history between a pitcher and catcher, particularly when considering how important game planning, preparation, and communication can be to a starting pitcher's success.

And Valdez could certainly use some additional help finding consistency.

The left-hander completed his first season with Detroit after signing a three-year, $115 million contract, but his performance didn't always match the expectations surrounding his arrival.

We previously highlighted how Valdez acknowledged the frustration of his difficult first season , even as he expressed satisfaction with remaining healthy and finishing the year on a positive note.

Maldonado's familiarity with Valdez's approach, preferences, and previous success could provide another resource for Detroit's coaching staff.

Of course, Maldonado wasn't hired specifically to serve as Valdez's personal coach, and there is no indication the Tigers are planning to change their pitching staff's responsibilities. However, bringing in someone who has worked closely with one of Detroit's highest-paid players certainly adds an intriguing dimension to the move.

The Tigers are also adding someone who has expressed a desire to eventually manage in the major leagues.

In discussing his interest in coaching after retirement, Maldonado explained his long-term ambition .

"My goal is to manage in the future," Maldonado said. "You've got to take it step by step."

Detroit presents an opportunity to gain experience under Hinch while contributing to a staff that needs to improve after missing the postseason.

Maldonado's extensive playing background could be particularly useful in game preparation, defensive planning, and communication with pitchers and catchers. He also joins an organization featuring Gold Glove catcher Dillon Dingler, giving Detroit another experienced voice with considerable knowledge of the position.

Exactly how the Tigers will use Maldonado's expertise remains to be seen, and the club has not formally announced the reported hiring.

Still, there is something encouraging about adding a former World Series champion who already has relationships with two important figures in the organization.

If Maldonado can help Hinch improve Detroit's preparation while providing valuable insight into Valdez, this could become one of the Tigers' more underrated offseason moves.

articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are headed to the World Series for the first time in 44 years, and the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel is rejoicing in the historic moment on its Saturday, Oct. 17 front page.

The cover celebrates the Brewers' National League Championship Series victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers, featuring beaming smiles and players celebrating after sweeping the series.

Brewers are going to World Series! See celebration, trophy presentation

The Brewers defeated the Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NLCS, securing their first World Series appearance since 1982 and giving Milwaukee fans another reason to celebrate.

Saturday's front page also features coverage from Journal Sentinel sports reporter Curt Hogg , highlighting the Brewers' historic journey to the World Series, including comments from NLCS MVP Jake Bauers, who said, " The city is ready ."

The historic victory marks just the second time in franchise history that the Brewers have advanced to the World Series. Their last appearance came in 1982, when Milwaukee faced the St. Louis Cardinals.

Readers can get a copy of the historic front page at local newsstands or delivered to their doorstep with a Milwaukee Journal Sentinel print subscription.

For longtime Brewers fans, the championship marks a milestone more than four decades in the making, bringing Milwaukee one step closer to its first World Series title.

Fans looking to commemorate the Brewers' World Series run can also purchase front-page prints, books and other keepsakes.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals injury report: Jeremiyah Love ruled out; Budda Baker questionable
articles.summary: Find out which Cardinals players won't play or might not play on Sunday against the Rams in Week 6.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals conducted their final practice of the week in preparation for Sunday's road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their final injury report of the week.

After not practicing all week, rookie running back Jeremiyah Love won't play against the Rams. Meanwhile, safety Budda Baker, who was on the report because of a rest day Wednesday, had a groin issue added on Friday and is questionable.

Outside linebacker Zaven Collins (hip), punter Blake Gillikin (back) and third quarterback Carson Beck (back) were added to the report Friday. Collins and Gillikin are also questionable.

Gillikin kicked only five games in 2025 because of a back injury, then suffered a groin injury in warmups prior to the Aug. 22 game against the Dallas Cowboys and kicker Chad Ryland handled the punting duties. In the preseason finale, Jack Browning was the punter. Gillikin has not been consistent this season and has a 45.6 average with a 38.0 net.

The full details of their final Week 6 injury report are below. After each player's injury, there is the daily status, which is either no status (NS), did not practice (DNP), limited (LIM) or FULL. Starters are noted with an asterisk.

*RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle): DNP, DNP, DNP

S Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion): DNP, DNP, DNP

*S Budda Baker (not injury related/rest/groin): DNP, FULL, DNP

S Kitan Crawford (ankle/practicing while on injured reserve): LIM, LIM, LIM

WR/RS Devin Duvernay (ribs): LIM, LIM, LIM

*LG Isaac Seumalo (not injury related/rest): DNP, FULL, NS

*OLB Josh Sweat (not injury related/rest): DNP, FULL, NS

WR Alex Bachman (wrist): LIM, FULL, FULL

*Tyler Higbee (not injury related/rest): NS, NS, DNP

*ILB Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder): LIM, LIM, FULL

*TE Colby Parkinson (shoulder): LIM, LIM, FULL

*ILB Omar Speights (knee): FULL, FULL, FULL

T/G Keagen Trost (hamstring/practicing while on injured reserve): NS, FULL, FULL

CB Josh Wallace (shoulder): LIM, LIM, FULL

*OLB Byron Young (not injury related/rest): NS, NS, DNP
